title: RFID Parking Token — NFC / UHF Barrier Credential
summary: RFID parking tokens are compact, coin-shaped NFC or UHF credentials for parking-facility access control, prepaid payment and vehicle identification — replacing paper tickets, magnetic-stripe cards and manual booth attendants with durable, rewritable electronic tokens. Aligned with ISO/IEC 14443-A/B, ISO/IEC 18092 NFC, NFC Forum Type 4 Tag Spec, EN 15291 / EN 12414 parking equipment, PCI DSS v4.0 for prepaid balances and GDPR / CCPA for parker data across SKIDATA, Designa, Amano McGann, TIBA, WPS, Scheidt & Bachmann, T2 Systems, ParkMobile and Flowbird estates.
heroPoints: Tap-and-go NFC per ISO/IEC 14443-A / NFC Forum Type 4 — 1-2 s barrier cycle at SKIDATA / Designa / WPS / Amano entry / exit readers, eliminating the 60 s queue that a jammed paper-ticket dispenser creates under EN 12414:2000 parking-control equipment stress.
Durable ABS / PC housing tested to IEC 60068-2-32 drop, -20 / +85 °C thermal cycle, IEC 60068-2-30 damp heat and ISO 4892-2 Cycle A dashboard UV for 10+ year service life.

NTAG424 DNA SUN AES-128 or MIFARE DESFire EV3 AES mutual authentication anti-clone — blocking the sidewalk key-copy attack that plain NTAG / Classic MIFARE tokens suffer, with PCI DSS v4.0 Req 3-4 and GDPR / CCPA-aware parker-data handling.

sections.title: Challenges parking operators, garage owners and city mobility teams face on RFID parking-token procurement

items.label: HF contactless cards + NFC Forum Type 4 Tag

bullets: Paper ticket dispensers jam, run out of stock and require daily maintenance under EN 12414:2000 parking-control-equipment reliability expectations. A single jammed dispenser backs up the entry lane in under 60 seconds, creating vehicle queues that spill onto public roads during peak arrival periods and trigger the operator-SLA penalties written into IPMI Accredited Parking Organization contracts and European Parking Association operator agreements.

Magnetic-stripe cards demagnetise from proximity to mobile phones, keys and wallets — 3-8% of monthly parkers report unreadable cards requiring replacement, generating helpdesk calls, barrier-lane disruptions and GDPR / CCPA parker-data re-registration events that expose the operator to data-minimisation complaints.

Paper tickets create ongoing consumable costs and labour for loading / maintaining dispensers; more importantly, operators working toward contactless-first mandates from city mobility authorities (TfL in London, RATP in Paris, MTA in NYC, Transport for NSW) are rejected at tender for facilities still reliant on single-use paper without an ISO/IEC 14443-conformant token programme.

Lost-ticket processing requires manual booth-attendant intervention, adding labour cost per incident and creating 2-5 minute delays per vehicle that back up exit lanes during evening peak — the same failure mode EN 15291:2007 Section 5 explicitly calls out as a service-level non-conformance for unattended barrier estates.

Parking operators managing multi-site portfolios need interoperable credentials that work across SKIDATA, Designa, Amano McGann, TIBA, WPS, Scheidt & Bachmann, T2 Systems, ParkMobile and Flowbird installations — and increasingly need transit-link (Calypso / ITSO / OV-chipkaart / Suica / Octopus) or tolling-link (E-ZPass, SunPass, FasTrak, via UHF) interoperability that plain 7-byte-UID NTAG tokens cannot provide.

sections.title: Applications for RFID parking tokens
bullets: Monthly and contract parking — issue reusable NTAG424 DNA SUN or DESFire EV3 tokens to monthly parkers, replacing magnetic cards and annual sticker renewals with a single durable credential under SKIDATA / Designa / WPS monthly-access templates.

Employee parking — distribute tokens to staff for automated barrier access at corporate, hospital (Joint Commission EC.02.01.01-adjacent), campus (FERPA-aware) and government (FIPS 201-3 PIV-compatible) parking structures.

Airport parking — long-term parking tokens with PCI DSS v4.0 tokenised prepaid balance for frequent travellers, integrated with loyalty and rewards programs via ParkMobile / PayByPhone / SKIDATA Guest Portal.

Municipal parking — city-wide parking token programs for residents and commuters, interoperable across multiple parking structures, surface lots and transit networks (Calypso in France / Belgium, ITSO in UK, OV-chipkaart in Netherlands, Suica in Japan, Octopus in Hong Kong).

Event and venue parking — issue pre-sold tokens for event attendees via Flowbird / ParkMobile, enabling express-lane entry and eliminating cash collection at the barrier under EN 12414 cash-handling exemption.

sections.title: Anatomy of the token — the coin, the coil, and the shell that outlives the barrier
sections.intro: A parking token is a coin you cannot spend: its whole job is to survive ten years of glovebox heat, keyring abuse and the occasional 1.5 m drop onto a garage deck, then open a barrier in about a second. The value sits in the layer between the antenna coil and the housing. The coin body is shared with the general-purpose [RFID coin tag](/products/rfid-tags/rfid-coin-tag/); the same credential in a wallet format is the [RFID parking card](/products/rfid-cards/rfid-parking-card/).

image.alt: Cutaway of a coin-shaped RFID parking token: a 304 / 316 stainless split ring, an ABS or polycarbonate housing UV-stable to ISO 4892-2, a 3-mil laser-engraved serial, a 13.56 MHz NFC coil antenna per ISO/IEC 14443-A, and a secure NTAG424 DNA / NTAG21x chip die, with a windshield UHF Monza R6-P / M775 variant reading 2-5 m at 860-960 MHz.

bullets: Housing: ABS (UL 94 V-0 flame-rated, drop-tested from 1.5 m onto concrete) or vandal-rated polycarbonate, UV-stable per ISO 4892-2 Cycle A for 1,000 h, with IP67 optional for exterior-kiosk returns.
NFC inlay: a 13.56 MHz antenna coil tuned per ISO/IEC 14443-3 / -4 carries an NTAG213 / NTAG215 / NTAG216 or NTAG424 DNA die — the silicon that answers every NFC-enabled barrier reader.
Memory: 144 B, 504 B or 888 B of user memory (NTAG213 / NTAG215 / NTAG216) or 416 B on NTAG424 DNA, holding parker ID, access zone, validity dates and prepaid balance for offline barrier operation.

Key-ring hole with a stainless split ring on the coin and fob SKUs; the windshield UHF variant swaps the ring for a PET adhesive label carrying a Monza R6-P or M775 inlay at 860-960 MHz for 2-5 m drive-through reads.
Laser serial: a 3-mil laser-engraved serial plus optional 4-colour logo gives the counter attendant a human-readable audit mark alongside the cryptographic UID.

sections.title: From bumper to boom gate — the one-second barrier cycle
sections.intro: Every parking token exists to answer one question at the barrier: is this car allowed in, right now, on this account? The token carries the credential, the parking-management system carries the verdict, and the boom gate just does what it is told. Here is the loop from the reader's point of view. To browse the adjacent form factors, see the full [RFID tag range](/products/rfid-tags/).

image.alt: Barrier-access flow: a driver taps the token 1-5 cm at the entry reader; the reader reads the 7-byte UID and an NTAG424 DNA SUN AES-128 CMAC; the parking-management system checks the access list online or offline; a valid credential opens the barrier in under 1 second and logs the pass, while a deactivated or expired token is refused and the attempt is logged.

bullets: Approach and tap: the driver holds the token within 1-5 cm of the entry reader; a 13.56 MHz ISO/IEC 14443 exchange reads the credential inside the 1-2 s barrier cycle — no ticket to pull, no card to swipe.

Read the credential: the reader lifts the factory 7-byte UID and, on secure SKUs, an NTAG424 DNA SUN message — an AES-128 CMAC-signed URL generated fresh on every tap that the server cryptographically verifies.

Check the access list: the parking-management system (SKIDATA ControlPanel, Designa Abacus, Amano McGann iParcNet, WPS ParkAdvance) validates the credential against the authorised database — online, or offline from the token's stored access zone and validity dates.
Grant or deny: a valid, active credential opens the barrier in under 1 second; a deactivated, expired or unrecognised token is refused and the attempt is logged for the operator.

Log and rotate: each pass writes a transaction record, and on NTAG424 DNA tokens the operator can rotate the per-site AES-128 key to invalidate any lost-token authenticator without reissuing the whole fleet.

faq.question: How long does an RFID parking token last?
faq.answer: The NFC chip has a 10-year data retention rating and supports 100,000 write cycles per NTAG / NTAG424 DNA / DESFire EV3 datasheet — more than sufficient for 10+ years of daily transaction logging. The ABS or polycarbonate housing is tested to IEC 60068-2-32 drop (1.5 m onto concrete), -20 / +85 °C thermal cycling per IEC 60068-2-1 / -2 and ISO 4892-2 Cycle A dashboard UV exposure. Unlike magnetic-stripe cards that demagnetise and paper tickets that are single-use under EN 12414:2000, the RFID token is a long-term reusable credential.

faq.question: Can tokens be transferred between vehicles?
faq.answer: By default, the token is linked to the parker account, not a specific vehicle, under GDPR / CCPA data-minimisation principles. It can be used with any vehicle driven by the authorised parker. For applications requiring vehicle-specific binding, the system can pair the token UID with a licence-plate number and validate both at the barrier using ANPR / LPR (Genetec AutoVu / Tattile / Neology) alongside the ISO/IEC 14443 read — a pattern common in corporate, hospital and airport estates.

faq.question: What happens if a token is lost or stolen?
faq.answer: The parking-management-system administrator (SKIDATA ControlPanel / Designa Abacus / Amano iParcNet / TIBA Smart Park / WPS ParkAdvance / Scheidt Entervo / T2 Luke) deactivates the lost token's UID in the authorised database. Any subsequent tap is rejected at the barrier. A replacement token with a new UID is issued and linked to the parker's account. Since the token itself stores no financial value by default (the balance is tokenised in the PCI DSS v4.0 server database), a lost token does not create a financial liability. For NTAG424 DNA tokens, the per-site AES-128 key can also be rotated to invalidate any lost-token cryptographic authenticator.

faq.question: Should I choose an NFC or a UHF parking token for barrier access?
faq.answer: For staff, tenant and monthly barrier access where the driver taps at the reader, choose the 13.56 MHz NFC token (NTAG213 / NTAG215 / NTAG216 or NTAG424 DNA per ISO/IEC 14443) — it reads at 1-5 cm and clears the barrier in the 1-2 s cycle. Choose the 860-960 MHz UHF windshield variant (Monza R6-P or M775) only for hands-free long-range lanes, where a 2-5 m read lets a VIP or residential vehicle trigger the gate without lowering a window. Most estates deploy NFC as the default and reserve UHF for premium or auto-open lanes.

faq.question: Will these tokens work with our existing SKIDATA / Designa / Amano barrier readers?
faq.answer: Yes. Parking tokens ship with factory block-write templates matched to SKIDATA ControlPanel, Designa Abacus, Amano McGann iParcNet, TIBA Smart Park, WPS ParkAdvance, Scheidt & Bachmann Entervo, T2 Systems Luke and Flowbird encoding schemes, so the credential is recognised by the barrier reader on day one. For legacy estates the MIFARE Classic 1K / 4K option matches installed SKIDATA / Designa / Amano readers; new deployments should specify NTAG424 DNA or MIFARE DESFire EV3 for cryptographic authentication. Confirm your controller model and firmware with us before the keyed lot so the block-write template is pre-approved.

faq.question: Can a parking token be cloned, and how is it secured?
faq.answer: A plain 7-byte-UID token can be read and copied at the kerb, which is why higher-risk portfolios specify a cryptographic SKU. The NTAG424 DNA SUN message generates an AES-128 CMAC-signed URL on every tap that the parking-management server verifies, and MIFARE DESFire EV3 adds AES-128 mutual authentication — both block the sidewalk key-copy attack that plain NTAG and MIFARE Classic tokens suffer. Per-site AES-128 key diversification with an HSM-backed key ceremony contains a compromised token to one site, and the per-site key can be rotated to invalidate any lost authenticator.
